layer_b_declaration.axis: The utterance asserts that inscription is the only available path between vision and reception — the voice's cost is encoded entirely in the command to write
layer_b_declaration.foreclosure: The source determines against direct transmission — the seer cannot speak to the seven assemblies; the book is the necessary and only medium

rotation.commentary: The primary joints: βλέπεις opened into the shadow-face of the utterance (pre-inscription beholding), γράψον εἰς βιβλίον encoded as cost-not-biography, and ἐπέστρεψα βλέπειν τὴν φωνήν collapsed hearing and sight into one disorienting receptive act — making the wager (body turned against prior orientation) structurally visible at the hinge between the two stanzas; χαλκολίβανος and πολλῶν each retained their strangeness (unnamed alloy, indeterminate plural) by carrying the bearing-cost directly into the shadow-register descriptions.
rotation.interpretation: Fire that consumes what it illuminates: the cost of the vision is the vision.

rite.speaker: Johannes Sigil
rite.text: The casting has arrived here: the first turn of John's body — the moment he turns to see the voice that is speaking to him, and finds not a face but seven lampstands, and in their midst the figure robed to the chest with a golden sash. The question is *how do I reach the writers* — and the rite has selected the verses where the command to write is already sounding, where the voice has already said *what you see, write into a book*, and where the seer has already turned. What the rotation will traverse in these verses is the axis of foreclosure: what John's turning cost, what remained behind him when he faced the lampstands, what the command to write suppressed in the act of commanding. Each operator will disclose a different bearing in the flesh of this passage — the eyes like flame, the feet like bronze fired in a kiln, the voice like many waters — and what was foreclosed when those images were fixed. The rite opens. Rebekah Cranes holds the first transform.
